› Write about 300 words explaining how TCP congestion control works, in plain …
  double each round-trip time. This lets TCP discover available capacity
  quickly. In classic TCP, once the window reaches a threshold, the sender
  switches to congestion avoidance and increases the window more gradually. TCP
  Reno, for example, grows its window by about one segment per round-trip time
  during this phase.

  When acknowledgments indicate that a segment is missing, TCP can retransmit it
  before a timer expires. In classic Reno, this kind of loss signal generally
  cuts the congestion window roughly in half. If a retransmission timer expires,
  the sender reduces the window more sharply and starts growing it again through
  slow start. When Explicit Congestion Notification is enabled, a router can
  mark packets to signal congestion before its queue overflows. The receiver
  relays that signal to the sender, which reduces its sending rate.
  The exact growth and slowdown rules depend on the congestion control
  algorithm. CUBIC grows its window as a function of time since the last
  congestion event. BBR estimates the path’s bottleneck bandwidth and round-trip
  propagation time to guide how quickly it sends.
